meta.name: Engineering, Robotics & Aerospace
meta.description: Robotics labs, semiconductor lithography & fab centers, aerospace propulsion hubs, engineering milestones, and domain guides.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

hubs.name: Chalmers Graphene Centre & 2D Materials
hubs.summary: Coordinator of the European Union's €1 billion Graphene Flagship—driving wafer-scale 2D semiconductor integration, spintronics, high-frequency graphene electronics, and structural carbon-composite batteries.

2D Spintronics & Structural Battery Composites

hubs.name: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)
hubs.summary: Managed by Caltech for NASA, JPL is humanity's flagship center for robotic deep-space exploration, operating the Deep Space Network and building Voyager 1 & 2, Perseverance, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and Europa Clipper.
hubs.nobel: Engineered the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space (Voyager) and the first powered aircraft to fly on another planet (Ingenuity on Mars, 72 flights).

rabbitLinks.reason: Operated directly by Caltech—connecting Pasadena's theoretical astrophysics and optics labs to interplanetary spacecraft.
Europa Clipper's search for a subsurface saltwater ocean mirrors WHOI's deep-sea hydrothermal vent exploration.
Transatlantic space partners co-building Earth observation satellites, Mars missions, and space gravitational-wave detectors.

projects.name: Europa Clipper & Mars Perseverance Rover
NASA Deep Space Network (DSN)

hubs.name: ESA ESTEC (European Space Research & Technology Centre)
hubs.summary: The European Space Agency's technical heart and largest establishment, housing the Large Space Simulator thermal-vacuum chamber and Concurrent Design Facility where Rosetta, Gaia, Euclid, Juice, and LISA are engineered and tested.
hubs.nobel: Engineered Europe's landmark missions including the first comet landing (Rosetta/Philae) and the 2-billion-star Gaia astrometry map.

rabbitLinks.reason: Just 25 km down the Dutch coast—TU Delft is ESTEC's closest academic partner for CubeSats and planetary entry.
ESTEC is engineering LISA (2.5-million-km laser interferometer in space) to extend LIGO's gravitational-wave window to supermassive black holes.

projects.name: LISA Space Gravitational-Wave Observatory
Euclid Dark-Universe Telescope & Juice Jupiter Mission

hubs.name: TU Delft Faculty of Aerospace Engineering
hubs.summary: Western Europe's largest aerospace engineering faculty, advancing blended-wing aircraft (Flying-V), liquid-hydrogen aviation, neuromorphic flapping-wing MAVLab drones, and student-built CubeSats.
hubs.nobel: Operates the SIMONA research flight simulator, Open Jet Wind Tunnel, and world-champion autonomous drone racing teams.

rabbitLinks.reason: 25 km from ESA's technical headquarters—Delft students and faculty design and test CubeSats and planetary landers directly with ESA.
Shares the TU Delft campus, linking aerospace communications with future satellite quantum key distribution.

projects.name: Flying-V Blended-Wing Aircraft & Hydrogen Aviation
MAVLab Neuromorphic Autonomous Drones

hubs.name: MIT Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AeroAstro)
hubs.summary: America's oldest aerospace engineering department—birthplace of the Apollo Guidance Computer (with Draper Lab), electrospray micro-thrusters, solid-state ionic-wind flight, and the MOXIE oxygen generator on Mars.
hubs.nobel: Built MOXIE aboard NASA Perseverance, demonstrating the first oxygen synthesis from another planet's atmosphere, and trained over 30 NASA astronauts.

rabbitLinks.reason: MIT AeroAstro's MOXIE instrument flew aboard JPL's Perseverance rover to manufacture breathable oxygen on Mars.
Jointly pioneers safe autonomous aerial swarms, formal verification for flight software, and space robotics.

projects.name: MOXIE Mars Oxygen ISRU & Space Propulsion Lab

hubs.name: Politecnico di Milano Engineering & Aerospace
hubs.summary: Italy's largest technical university, excelling in deep-space CubeSat astrodynamics (ESA Hera/Milani & LUMIO), autonomous high-speed racing (PoliMOVE), rotorcraft aeroelasticity, and integrated quantum photonics.

rabbitLinks.reason: PoliMi's DART Lab designs autonomous optical navigation for ESA's Hera/Milani asteroid-defense CubeSats.

projects.name: Deep-Space CubeSat Astrodynamics (Milani / LUMIO)
PoliMOVE Autonomous Racing Platform

hubs.name: NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center
hubs.summary: NASA's primary atmospheric flight-research testbed on Rogers Dry Lakebed, birthplace of supersonic flight (X-1), hypersonic rocket planes (X-15), digital fly-by-wire avionics, and the quiet-supersonic X-59 Quesst demonstrator.

projects.name: X-59 Quesst Quiet Supersonic Technology Aircraft
Subsonic Sustainable Flight Demonstrator

hubs.summary: Germany's largest aerospace research campus near Munich, operating the German Space Operations Center (GSOC), ESA's Columbus ISS Control Center, synthetic-aperture radar satellites (TanDEM-X), and atmospheric research aircraft.

projects.name: German Space Operations Center (GSOC) & Columbus Control
TanDEM-X & Next-Gen Bistatic Radar Earth Observation

hubs.name: ONERA (The French Aerospace Lab)
hubs.summary: France's national aerospace research center operating Europe's premier transonic and hypersonic wind tunnels (Modane-Avrieux), advancing green propulsion, adaptive space optics, and orbital debris tracking radar (GRAVES).

projects.name: DRAGON Hybrid-Electric Distributed Propulsion Concept
Space Electrostatic Accelerometers & GRAVES Space Surveillance

hubs.name: JAXA Chofu Aerospace Center
hubs.summary: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's hub for aeronautical technology, propulsion, and aerodynamic supercomputing, housing transonic/hypersonic wind tunnels, electric-propulsion testbeds, and the JSS3 aerospace supercomputer.

hubs.name: ISRO Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)

projects.name: Gaganyaan Human Spaceflight & Crew Escape System
Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) & RLV Reusable Demonstrator

hubs.name: ISAE-SUPAERO
hubs.summary: The world's first dedicated aerospace engineering school, anchored in Toulouse's Aerospace Valley and leading European research in turbomachinery, autonomous flight, Martian acoustics (SuperCam microphone), and sustainable aviation.

hubs.name: Rolls-Royce Civil Aerospace & UltraFan R&D

projects.name: UltraFan Geared High-Bypass Aero Engine Demonstrator

hubs.name: Blue Origin
hubs.summary: Orbital launch and space-infrastructure engineering firm developing oxygen-rich staged-combustion methalox rocket engines (BE-4), the reusable heavy-lift New Glenn launch vehicle, and the Blue Moon lunar lander.

projects.name: New Glenn Heavy-Lift Reusable Orbital Rocket & BE-4 Engine
Blue Moon Mk1 & Mk2 Lunar Lander Program

hubs.name: ITA (Aeronautics Institute of Technology) & DCTA
hubs.summary: Latin America's premier aerospace engineering institute modeled on MIT within Brazil's Department of Aerospace Science and Technology (DCTA), catalyzing Embraer's global commercial aviation industry and Brazil's satellite and hypersonic programs.

hubs.name: CEA-Leti (Microelectronics & Nanotechnologies)

hubs.nobel: Generated over 3,200 patents and 75+ deep-tech spinouts including Soitec, Lynred, and Siquance quantum processors.

hubs.name: Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology (SAIT)

Loihi 2 Neuromorphic Spiking Neural Processors

rabbitLinks.reason: Co-built the Morello prototype processor implementing Cambridge's CHERI memory-safe hardware capabilities.

rabbitLinks.reason: Mumbai's twin science-and-engineering pillars—linking fundamental physics & math in Colaba with nanofabrication in Powai.

hubs.name: NY CREATES / Albany NanoTech Complex

hubs.name: Fraunhofer IPMS (Photonic Microsystems)

hubs.name: UCSB Solid State Lighting & Energy Electronics Center (SSLEEC)
hubs.summary: Co-directed by Nobel laureate Shuji Nakamura and Steven DenBaars, SSLEEC is the global epicenter of gallium-nitride (GaN) and wide-bandgap III-nitride semiconductors for micro-LED displays, laser lighting, and high-efficiency power electronics.

hubs.name: Applied Materials Maydan Technology Center (MTC)
hubs.summary: The semiconductor industry's flagship materials-engineering and wafer-equipment R&D laboratory, developing atomic-layer deposition, selective epitaxy, plasma etch, and electron-beam metrology systems used inside virtually every advanced fab on Earth.

SoftBots & Rehab Technologies Wearable Prosthetics

ARCHES Autonomous Multi-Robot Planetary Exploration

ModLab Modular & Dynamic Legged Robotics

events.title: The Antikythera Mechanism: Ancient Geared Astronomical Computer
events.summary: An intricate hand-powered bronze clockwork assembly of at least 30 interlocking precision gears calculating solar/lunar positions, lunar anomaly via epicyclic gearing, eclipse cycles (Saros), and Olympiad dates.
events.impact: Stands as the earliest known analog mechanical computer, revealing astonishing Hellenistic precision metallurgy and gear engineering unmatched for over a millennium.

events.title: Gutenberg Movable-Type Printing Press
events.summary: Combined durable lead-tin-antimony alloy movable type, oil-based ink, and a mechanical screw press to mass-produce accurate books at a fraction of scribal cost.
events.impact: Enabled rapid, reproducible dissemination of scientific diagrams, mathematical tables, and experimental findings across Europe—igniting the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: James Watt's Separate-Condenser Steam Engine Powers Industry
events.summary: By adding an external condenser and later rotary sun-and-planet gearing plus the centrifugal flyball governor, James Watt slashed coal consumption by ~75% compared to Newcomen atmospheric engines.
events.impact: Catalyzed the Industrial Revolution, inspired Sadi Carnot's laws of thermodynamics, and introduced feedback control engineering via the mechanical governor.

events.title: Wright Brothers Achieve Powered, Controlled Heavier-Than-Air Flight
events.location: Kitty Hawk, NC (designed in Dayton, OH)
events.summary: After building their own wind tunnel to measure 200+ airfoil shapes and inventing three-axis aerodynamic control (pitch, roll via wing-warping, yaw), flew the Wright Flyer on December 17, 1903.
events.impact: Launched aerospace engineering, shrinking global travel from weeks to hours and establishing systematic wind-tunnel aerodynamics.

events.title: Robert Goddard Launches the First Liquid-Fueled Rocket
events.summary: Fired a liquid-oxygen and gasoline rocket 41 feet into the sky on March 16, 1926, later pioneering gyroscopic guidance, gimbaled thrust vanes, and turbopumps for spaceflight propulsion.
events.impact: Demonstrated the high-specific-impulse liquid-propellant architecture underlying every modern orbital launcher from Saturn V to Falcon 9 and Starship.

events.title: ENIAC: First Programmable Electronic General-Purpose Computer
events.figure: J. Presper Eckert, John Mauchly & ENIAC Programmers
events.summary: Completed at the University of Pennsylvania using nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes—programmed by six pioneering women mathematicians (Kay McNulty, Betty Jennings, Betty Snyder, Marlyn Wescoff, Fran Bilas, Ruth Lichterman)—computing thousands of times faster than electromechanical relays.
events.impact: Demonstrated high-speed electronic digital computing and directly catalyzed the von Neumann stored-program architecture.

events.title: Invention of the Semiconductor Transistor at Bell Labs
events.figure: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain & William Shockley
events.summary: Demonstrated the first solid-state point-contact germanium transistor amplifying electrical signals without fragile, power-hungry vacuum tubes.
events.impact: Became the fundamental atomic-scale switch of the Information Age—today exceeding 100 billion transistors per AI chip.

events.title: Invention of the Monolithic Integrated Circuit (Microchip)
events.summary: Jack Kilby (Texas Instruments) built the first working germanium IC in 1958, while Robert Noyce (Fairchild Semiconductor) created the planar silicon integrated circuit in 1959 suited for mass photolithography.
events.impact: Unleashed Moore's Law—shrinking room-sized computers into smartphones, spacecraft guidance systems, and AI data centers.

events.title: Apollo 11 Crewed Moon Landing & Real-Time Flight Software
events.figure: NASA, Saturn V Engineers, Margaret Hamilton & Apollo 11 Crew
events.summary: Combined the Saturn V super-heavy launch vehicle, lunar-orbit rendezvous astrodynamics, and MIT's priority-scheduled Apollo Guidance Computer software to land humans safely on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
events.impact: Catalyzed integrated-circuit reliability, real-time software engineering, systems engineering, and human deep-space exploration.

events.title: Launch of the Global Argo Autonomous Ocean Observing Array
events.figure: Dean Roemmich, International Argo Science Team (Scripps / WHOI / JAMSTEC)
events.summary: Deployed an international fleet of ~4,000 robotic battery-powered profiling floats drifting across every ice-free ocean basin, diving to 2,000 meters every 10 days and beaming temperature, salinity, and biogeochemical data via satellite.
events.impact: Revolutionized operational oceanography and proved Earth's oceans absorb over 90% of planetary warming heat imbalance, feeding real-time climate and weather models.

events.title: First Propulsive Landing of an Orbital-Class Rocket Booster
events.summary: On December 21, 2015, after boosting 11 satellites toward orbit, a Falcon 9 first stage flipped in space, executed hypersonic supersonic retropropulsion, and landed upright at Landing Zone 1.
events.impact: Shattered the 60-year paradigm of expendable orbital rockets, cutting launch costs dramatically and enabling global satellite constellations and rapid space science.

events.title: Deployment of High-NA EUV Lithography (0.55 NA) for Angstrom Chips
events.figure: ASML, ZEISS SMT & imec Lithography Teams
events.summary: ASML delivered and printed first 8-nanometer features with Twinscan EXE:5000 High-NA Extreme Ultraviolet scanners combining laser-produced tin-plasma 13.5 nm light with anamorphic ZEISS atomic-smooth mirrors.
events.impact: Extends sub-2 nm semiconductor scaling into the angstrom era, enabling next-generation energy-efficient AI accelerators, photonics, and scientific supercomputers.

stops.title: TSMC Global R&D Center
stops.bridge: TSMC etches 100-billion-transistor silicon dies and stitches them via CoWoS 3D packaging to manufacture NVIDIA's flagship AI GPUs.

stops.title: NVIDIA Research
stops.bridge: Massive coherent clusters of NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs supply the petaflops of matrix multiplication that train OpenAI's frontier models.

stops.title: OpenAI

stops.title: Anthropic (Mechanistic Interpretability)
stops.bridge: Closes the loop by peering back inside silicon-hosted transformers with sparse autoencoders to map the hidden circuits of machine cognition.

trails.title: From Abyssal Seafloor Vents to Alien Ocean Worlds
trails.tagline: Discover how mapping Earth's hidden ocean floor transformed our search for extraterrestrial life and cosmic waves.

stops.title: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
stops.bridge: Marie Tharp and Bruce Heezen drew the first global ocean-floor maps here, exposing the 40,000-mile mid-ocean volcanic ridge that proved plate tectonics.

stops.title: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
stops.bridge: Diving down to those volcanic ridges in submersible Alvin in 1977, WHOI discovered sunless chemosynthetic life thriving on hydrothermal vents.

stops.title: Scripps Institution of Oceanography
stops.bridge: Expanded global ocean-atmosphere sensing via the Keeling Curve and 4,000 autonomous Argo floats—honing remote sensing for icy planetary oceans.

stops.title: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
stops.bridge: Directly inspired by Earth's hydrothermal vents, JPL engineered Europa Clipper to probe Jupiter's moon for a warm, life-supporting subsurface saltwater ocean.

stops.title: ESA ESTEC
stops.bridge: Europe's technical space hub launched Juice toward Jupiter's icy moons and is now engineering the 2.5-million-km LISA laser interferometer in space.

stops.title: LIGO Observatory
stops.bridge: Proved gravitational-wave interferometry on Earth—paving the way for ESA/NASA's space-borne LISA to hear supermassive black holes collide across cosmic time.

trails.title: From Living Brain Circuits to Agile Humanoid Machines
trails.tagline: Trace the feedback loop from silicon neural probes and biological connectomes to Vision-Language-Action robots.

stops.title: HHMI Janelia Research Campus
stops.bridge: Mapped the complete fruit-fly brain connectome and co-engineered Neuropixels silicon probes (with imec) to record thousands of living neurons at once.

stops.title: Allen Institute for Brain Science
stops.bridge: Scaled open brain mapping to 5,300+ mammalian cell types and cortical connectomes, fueling computational theories of biological learning.

stops.title: Vector Institute (Toronto)
stops.bridge: Geoffrey Hinton turned brain-inspired artificial neural networks and backpropagation into AlexNet (2012), igniting modern deep learning.

stops.title: UC Berkeley BAIR
stops.bridge: Extended deep neural networks from pixels to physical action via deep reinforcement learning and open cross-embodiment robot manipulation datasets.

stops.title: Physical Intelligence (π)
stops.bridge: Co-founded by Berkeley and Stanford roboticists to train generalist Vision-Language-Action policies capable of folding laundry and manipulating tools.

stops.title: Boston Dynamics
stops.bridge: Pairs emerging AI dexterity with decades of dynamic whole-body hardware mastery culminating in the all-electric Atlas humanoid.

stops.title: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab
stops.bridge: Demonstrates how massively parallel GPU reinforcement learning trains rugged legged robots in minutes to hike Alpine mountains and lunar craters.

trails.title: Mapping the Living Brain
trails.tagline: Journey from foundational synaptic biology and the first worm connectome to silicon Neuropixels probes and brain-spine interfaces.

stops.title: Institut Pasteur (Paris)

stops.title: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
stops.bridge: Sydney Brenner and John White mapped the first complete nervous system in history—every neuron and synapse of the nematode C. elegans—proving whole-brain connectomics was possible.

stops.title: imec Leuven (Neuropixels Silicon)
stops.bridge: Repurposed CMOS semiconductor lithography to fabricate hair-thin Neuropixels probes packed with hundreds of electrodes recording thousands of live neurons simultaneously.

stops.title: HHMI Janelia Research Campus

stops.title: Allen Institute for Brain Science

stops.title: EPFL AI & Neuro-X Ecosystem
stops.bridge: Synthesizes large-scale neural simulation and real-time AI decoding into wireless brain-spine interfaces that restore voluntary walking after spinal cord injury.

stops.title: Rocket Lab
